image_description: A group of sea lions resting on wooden floating docks. Several individuals are visible, primarily brown in color, with sleek, wet-looking fur. One sea lion in the center is curled up sleeping, while another to its right rests its head on the wood. In the background, another sea lion lies on a higher dock section. The scene is set in a harbor environment with water visible between the docks.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible heads belong to females or juveniles which lack the prominent sagittal crest and thick neck mane characteristic of adult males. The heads are smooth and rounded.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small but distinct external ear flaps are visible on the heads of the sea lions (e.g., the one in the center), confirming they are otariids (sea lions) rather than phocids (true seals).
Dark, stiff whiskers are clearly visible protruding from the snouts of the animals, particularly the central figure.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bodies are torpedo-shaped (fusiform) and robust, fitting the description of large marine mammals.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreflippers are visible on several animals, appearing large and paddle-like. While the 'hairless underside' is hard to verify definitively due to pose, the general morphology is correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hind flippers are mostly tucked under the body or obscured by the angle and other animals. Their ability to rotate cannot be visually verified in this static resting pose.
Despite the relaxed poses, the underlying anatomical structure of the animals shows clear bilateral symmetry.
